gh pr create --title "feat(server,core): report relationship-type purpose on list and get" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## What

Classifying `member_of` as authorization-bearing (#2833) made every write action on it 403 via `assertNotAuthorizationType`. Nothing on a **read** path said so.

`rtHandleList` and `rtHandleGet` select explicit column lists that omitted `rt.purpose` — it was selected only on guard/write paths (`:868`, `:900`, `:916`, `:1356`, `:1376`). So a client could not distinguish an authorization-bearing type from an ordinary org-owned one, and `member_of` **is** org-owned, so ownership alone cannot separate them. Owletto rendered Delete and Add Rule on it, both guaranteed to fail.

## How

Adds `purpose` to `list` and `get`, and also to `create` and `update` so the row shape does not vary by action — a client switching on the field must not see it appear and disappear.

Contract field is optional and nullable, so an older client is unaffected. Left an open string rather than a literal union so a server that learns a new purpose does not fail contract validation against a cached client schema.

Owletto companion: lobu-ai/owletto#881 (hold until this is green, then merge, then repin).

## Verification

```
authorization-type-guards.test.ts    Tests  14 passed (14)
packages/server tsc --noEmit         exit 0
packages/core   tsc --noEmit         exit 0
Depot full remote preflight          passed (tree f007771f)
```

Three new cases, each **mutation-tested**:

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| drop `rt.purpose` from LIST select | `reports purpose on LIST` fails — `expected undefined to be 'authorization'` |
| drop `rt.purpose` from GET select | `reports purpose on GET too` fails — same |
| drop from create+update selects | LIST + UPDATE fail (2 failed / 12 passed) |

Assertions use `toHaveProperty("purpose", null)` rather than `?? null` — the loose form still passes once a handler stops selecting the column, so it would not have caught the regression.

## Generated client

Regenerated against the booted server, not hand-edited:

```
cd packages/client && LOBU_OPENAPI_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9533/lobu/api/docs/openapi.json bun run generate
```

Delta is exactly `purpose?: string | null;` at all four emitted `RelationshipTypeRow` sites. `[client-regen-not-needed]` does **not** apply — the emitted schema genuinely changes.

## Known gap, deliberately not in scope

The **edge** surface still has the same problem: `RelationshipRowSchema` (`manage-entity.ts:321`) carries `relationship_type_slug` but no purpose, so a client listing an entity's relationships still cannot predict which unlink buttons 403. That needs a shape decision rather than a column — `purpose` alone is the wrong predictor there, because the edge guard is slug-**OR**-purpose, and a freshly declared unclassified `member_of` reads `purpose: null` and still refuses. A derived boolean is probably right. Separate PR.

Same class, different contract: `workspace-instructions.ts:88` renders relationship types into agent prompt text with no purpose, so an agent will still attempt writes that 403.
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -2

**Shipped this round**

Three things worth flagging, since two were my mistakes.

**I ran `biome check --write .` in the Owletto repo without its config** and reformatted 370 files. Only your "stage by explicit path" rule kept the commit clean — but `relationship-types-tab.tsx` still went in with 941 reformatted lines against a ~20-line real change. Nothing else in that repo was touched; working tree is clean at `origin/main` + one commit.

**The flake's cause was not what I first said.** I claimed an 80ms margin against timer drift. Wrong — a 5ms margin still passed locally, and CPU saturation at load 47 passed 6/6, because starving the event loop delays the poll and the claim equally. It's **database** latency: `pg_sleep(0.2)` in `claim()` made it fail 3/3 deterministically, and the fix holds 3/3 there and at 0.35. That correction is in the commit message and PR body.

**review-fix caught a real weakness in my tests.** I wrote `expect(x?.purpose ?? null).toBeNull()`, which passes even if the key disappears — it would not have caught the regression it was meant to guard. It rewrote them to `toHaveProperty("purpose", null)` and added an UPDATE case for SELECTs I'd changed without covering. I mutation-tested all three: dropping the column from LIST, GET, and create+update each kills exactly the intended assertion.

Also confirmed rather than assumed: the generated client genuinely needed regenerating (contract path is watched, `[client-regen-not-needed]` doesn't apply). I booted the server and regenerated — exact delta was `purpose?: string | null;` at all four sites.

Untouched, as I said I'd leave it: your uncommitted preview-env work in the main checkout, and #2826.

description: "make pre-pr-remote derives its patch base from origin/<branch>, NOT local HEAD — rebasing without pushing first gates a stale tree and produces phantom failures in files that no longer exist"
metadata:

---

`make pre-pr-remote` prints its base in the header. It is the **REMOTE** branch:

```
Base: origin/feat/public-ghcr-images
Merge base: 8f46ff2565…
Patch size: 4936561 bytes
Cache key: patch/8f46ff256571/…
```

**So a local rebase that has not been pushed gates the OLD tree.** Hit 2026-08-17
on lobu#2779: rebased a 2-line `charts/lobu/values.yaml` change onto current main,
gated without pushing, and got **8 failed jobs**, including `format-lint` failing
twice on retired-vocabulary hits:

```
packages/server/src/watchers/reaction-executor.ts:1: retired term in path
packages/server/src/worker-api/behavior-trigger.ts:1: retired term in path
```

Those paths exist in **neither** `origin/main` nor the worktree — the #2784 rename
deleted them. The gate had reconstructed 8/15's tree from the stale remote head.

**The tell:** failures naming files you cannot find locally. Check the header's
`Base:`/`Merge base:` before debugging anything else, and confirm with
`git ls-tree -r --name-only origin/main -- <path>` (empty = absent).

**Fix:** `git push --force-with-lease origin HEAD:<branch>` FIRST, then gate.

Same family as [[reference_two_pr_gate_false_positives_from_a_stale_base]] — a
stale base is the single most common source of phantom gate failures here.

## Also: `pkill -f "make pre-pr-remote"` is a LOADED GUN
Other Claude sessions on this machine run gates too (theirs log to different
paths, e.g. `/tmp/prpr2.log`, and carry a different `/tmp/claude-<id>-cwd`).
`pkill -f` would kill a teammate's 20-minute gate with no warning. Kill the
specific PID instead. And since Depot serializes org-wide, always check for a
live peer before dispatching — a new dispatch silently cancels theirs
([[feedback_check_for_a_peer_session_on_the_pr_queue]],
[[reference_pgrep_pre_pr_remote_matches_itself]]).

In **lobu** the incantation is
`biome check --config-path config/biome.config.json --write .`
([[feedback_biome_via_check_fix]]). Carrying that habit into
`packages/owletto` is wrong twice over: owletto has **no `biome.json`** of its
own and its package script is just

```json
"lint": "biome lint src"
```

Running `bunx biome check --write .` there on 2026-08-17 rewrote **370 files** —
`apps/chrome/**`, `apps/mac/**`, k8s dashboards, `src/**`, config — because it
fell back to defaults and formatted the whole repo.

**What saved it:** staging by explicit path, so the commit held only the 4
intended files. But the damage still leaked in: `relationship-types-tab.tsx` was
committed with **941 changed lines** against a ~20-line real edit, because the
file had already been reformatted before `git add`. The diffstat is the tell —
if a file's line count dwarfs your edit, the formatter got there first.

**Recovery that worked:** `git reset --hard origin/main`, re-apply the change,
re-verify. (A hard reset was safe ONLY because the work also existed as a saved
patch + per-file backups in the scratchpad — never do it otherwise,
[[feedback_never_git_checkout_to_undo_a_mutation]].) Note a hard reset also
discards edits made after the patch was captured; those had to be redone.

**Rule:** inside owletto, lint only the files you touched —
`bunx biome lint <paths>` — and never `--write .`.

# Browser-driven verification (authenticated)

For any UI verification that needs a signed-in session (past the auth wall), mint a session cookie from the DB and drive the **paired Owletto extension** through the Lobu connector-operations bridge (`lobu call manage_operations`, or the SDK `operations` namespace). This runs in the user's real logged-in Chrome — no separate headless browser, no CDP, no extra browser tooling to install.

## Scope

The forged session cookie authenticates the **web admin REST mounted at `/`** (`/api/auth/*`, `/api/<orgSlug>/...`, the SPA — anything `lobu apply` and the web app talk to). It does **NOT** authenticate the **public Agent API at `/lobu`** (`/lobu/api/v1/agents/*`, `/lobu/api/v1/agents/<id>/sessions`) — that path expects a JWT bearer from the OAuth device flow (`lobu login`) or a PAT. If `/lobu/api/v1/agents` returns `401` despite a valid cookie, switch to `lobu chat` / `lobu token`.

## Pick a target

Local dev backend (with prod DB attached over Tailscale): `https://<your-tailscale-host>.ts.net:8443`. Prod: `https://app.lobu.ai`.

## Grab the secret + session token

```bash
# Local dev backend uses .env's BETTER_AUTH_SECRET
SECRET=$(grep '^BETTER_AUTH_SECRET=' .env | cut -d= -f2-)

# Prod uses the secret on the K8s pod
SECRET=$(kubectl exec -n summaries-prod \
  $(kubectl get pod -n summaries-prod -l app.kubernetes.io/name=lobu-app -o name | head -1 | sed 's|pod/||') \
  -- printenv BETTER_AUTH_SECRET)
```

Session token from the DB. With no local `DATABASE_URL` set, exec psql inside the prod DB pod (the prod DB serves both targets):

```bash
DBURL=$(kubectl exec -n summaries-prod <lobu-app-pod> -- printenv DATABASE_URL)
PGPASS=$(printf '%s' "$DBURL" | sed -E 's#.*://[^:]+:([^@]+)@.*#\1#')
TOKEN=$(kubectl exec -n summaries-prod lobu-ai-prod-db-1 -- \
  env PGPASSWORD="REDACTED" psql -h lobu-ai-prod-db-pooler -U summaries -d owletto -tAc \
  "SELECT token FROM session WHERE \"userId\" = '<user_id>' AND \"expiresAt\" > NOW() ORDER BY \"updatedAt\" DESC LIMIT 1")
```

## Sign the cookie

better-auth uses HMAC-SHA256, base64, then URL-encode — base64**url** does *not* validate.

```bash
SIGNED=$(SECRET="$SECRET" TOKEN="$TOKEN" node -e '
  const {createHmac}=require("node:crypto");
  const sig=createHmac("sha256",process.env.SECRET).update(process.env.TOKEN).digest("base64");
  console.log(encodeURIComponent(`${process.env.TOKEN}.${sig}`));
')
```

Cookie name is `__Secure-better-auth.session_token` whenever the baseURL is `https://` (prod and Tailscale dev qualify; only plain-http localhost uses the unprefixed `better-auth.session_token`).

## Find the Chrome connection

Browser actions dispatch to a paired Chrome extension connection (usually org `buremba`):

```bash
lobu call manage_connections --org buremba --arg action=list --raw
```

Pick the `chrome` connector with `status: active` on the machine whose browser you want to drive. `operations.listAvailable({ connection_id })` reports per-target `readiness` and `execution_targets` — use it to check the device is actually online before a long verification.

## Drive the browser

Multi-step verifications are one `run_sdk` script (the tab id threads through every call):

```bash
lobu call run_sdk --arg script='
export default async (ctx, client) => {
  const CHROME = <chrome-connection-id>;
  const COOKIE = "<SIGNED>";
  // 1. Open the app origin in a fresh background tab.

input.content:
UI proof · lobu#2839 · owletto#881

Authorization-bearing relationship types stop offering writes

Arming the ACL guard made every write on member_of return 403. The settings tab and the relationship picker kept rendering edit affordances for it — buttons that were guaranteed to fail. This is the before/after for the Owletto pointer move that fixes them.

Parent PR
lobu-ai/lobu#2839 (submodule pointer bump)
Owletto PR
lobu-ai/owletto#881
Before
a25f5a7cbbb675c5cad0143719c587e0bd31b029
After
90c55a8825eede18b93a71a609b8959260627aa9
Captured on
one booted local instance, lobu 2ea1e6c4 (server + DB fixed across both sides)
Surface
/<org>/entity-types/person → "Relationships"

The data both sides ran against

Identical on both sides: the same Postgres rows, read back through the same server build via manage_entity_schema action: list. Only the frontend pointer moved between captures. The purpose column is what the server started returning in lobu#2837.

slugnameorganization_slugstatuspurpose
member_ofMember oflocal-installactiveauthorization
reports_toReports tolocal-installactivenull
works_atWorks atlocal-installactivenull

All three are owned by the viewing org and all three are active — so ownership and status cannot tell them apart. purpose is the only field that separates the type the server refuses to modify from the two it accepts.

Surface 1 — the entity type's Relationships section

Rendered structure extracted from the live component tree at each pointer, fed the payload above.

Before a25f5a7c
Member ofmember_of
this→Team×
Reports toreports_to
this→Person×
Works atworks_at
this→Company×
After 90c55a88
Reports toreports_to
this→Person×
Works atworks_at
this→Company×
Managed by access control

this→Teamno remove

The extraction, verbatim

Machine-read from the rendered DOM — section headings, per-type badges, and the number of buttons each type's rule rows expose.

BEFORE  a25f5a7c
headings: []

Member of   member_of
  badges:        []
  removeButtons: 1
Reports to  reports_to
  badges:        []
  removeButtons: 1
Works at    works_at
  badges:        []
  removeButtons: 1
AFTER   90c55a88
headings: ["Managed by access control"]

Reports to  reports_to
  badges:        []
  removeButtons: 1
Works at    works_at
  badges:        []
  removeButtons: 1
Member of   member_of
  badges:        ["read-only"]
  removeButtons: 0

The two ordinary types are untouched in both columns — one remove button each, no badge. Only member_of moves: it gains the read-only badge, loses its remove button, and lands under a new heading. It stays visible, so nothing disappears from the operator's view.

Surface 2 — the "new relationship" picker

Before the change the picker offered member_of; choosing it produced a form whose save was guaranteed to 403. The merged test asserts the type is absent — running that same spec against both pointers:

Before a25f5a7c
× offers local relationship types
  and every mapped entity type

AssertionError: expected document
not to contain element, found
  <span> Member of

  111| expect(screen.queryByText("Member of"))
       .not.toBeInTheDocument();

Tests  1 failed | 2 passed (3)
After 90c55a88
✓ uses distinct field ids when responsive
  presentations coexist
✓ offers local relationship types
  and every mapped entity type
✓ retries only add_rule when creating
  the type succeeded first

What changed in the source

relationship-types-tab.tsx
-  const localTypes = activeTypes.filter(
-    (rt) => !rt.organization_slug || rt.organization_slug === orgContext?.slug
-  );
+  const ownedTypes = activeTypes.filter(
+    (rt) => !rt.organization_slug || rt.organization_slug === orgContext?.slug
+  );
+  const localTypes = ownedTypes.filter((rt) => rt.purpose !== PURPOSE_AUTHORIZATION);
+  const accessManagedTypes = ownedTypes.filter(
+    (rt) => rt.purpose === PURPOSE_AUTHORIZATION
+  );

new-relationship-form.tsx
   const activeTypes = relationshipTypes.filter(
     (rt: RelationshipType) =>
       rt.status === "active" &&
+      rt.purpose !== PURPOSE_AUTHORIZATION &&
       (!rt.organization_slug || rt.organization_slug === orgContext?.slug),
   );

The predicate is purpose, never the slug. The server keeps slug matching behind an explicit includeSlug flag precisely because it drifts, so a client that hardcoded slug === 'member_of' would diverge the moment a second authorization type appears.

How this was captured

One booted instance of lobu 2ea1e6c4 with its own Postgres, seeded once with the three relationship types and their rules. member_of was classified purpose = 'authorization' the way the connector ACL syncs do it, under lobu.acl_write. The server and the database were never restarted or re-seeded between the two sides — only packages/owletto was moved from a25f5a7c to 90c55a88, with Vite HMR re-rendering the running page in place.

The page was confirmed rendering in a real browser at both pointers, against that instance. The structural extraction above and the picker spec runs are the reproducible record of what each pointer renders.

One limit worth stating. This page carries the extracted DOM structure and the red/green spec runs, not browser screenshots — screenshot export was not available in the session that produced it. Everything here is reproducible in about a minute: boot the instance, seed the three types, and load /<org>/entity-types/person at each pointer.

Still not covered by this change

Stated so a reviewer does not read the fix as broader than it is. The edge surface is still blind: RelationshipRowSchema carries relationship_type_slug but nothing that predicts a 403, so unlink buttons on an entity's relationships can still fail. purpose alone is the wrong predictor there — the edge guard is slug-or-purpose, so a freshly declared, unclassified member_of reads purpose: null and is still refused. That needs a derived boolean and a contract decision. Agent-facing instruction text has the same gap.

---
name: reference_ui_review_artifact_requires_a_hosted_before_after
description: "An owletto pointer bump whose range touches src/ cannot pass ui-review as not-applicable — it needs ARTIFACT=<hosted https before/after>, and the recipe for producing one is: hold server+DB fixed, swap only the submodule SHA, let Vite HMR re-render"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
---

`make ui-review` has exactly two passing paths (`scripts/ui-review.ts`):

1. **Not applicable** — the Owletto range is `ahead` AND `isDeployOnlyRange(files)`. Pure
   `deploy/` diffs only.
2. **Proof recorded** — `ARTIFACT=<https url>` is published as a comment on the
   **merged** Owletto PR and mirrored onto the parent lobu PR.

There is no third path. A pointer bump touching `src/` **will** fail
`make bump` at the last step with `error: UI proof is required; rerun in
<worktree> with: make ui-review ARTIFACT=<https-url>` — the PR, the commit
and `pi-review` are already posted by then, so just finish it in that worktree.

## The recipe that works
`scripts/lib/ui-review-proof.ts` states the bar in the comment body it writes:
*"captured from one booted instance against the same data on both sides."*
Satisfy it literally:

1. `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` — its owletto is pinned at the **BEFORE** SHA.
2. `make dev`, then seed via psql. Vite runs in **middleware mode on the same
   port** — there is no separate vite port, and `/` 404s for `curl` unless you
   send `Accept: text/html`.
3. Capture BEFORE.
4. `git -C packages/owletto checkout <AFTER-sha>` — **Vite HMR re-renders the
   running page in place.** Server, DB and data never move, which is exactly
   what the proof text claims.
5. Capture AFTER, publish an artifact, `make ui-review ARTIFACT=<url>`.

Local dev auto-authenticates (`src/lib/use-local-install-auto-signin.ts`), so a
plain `open <url>` lands on the page already signed in. For API calls:
`POST /api/local-init` with header `X-Lobu-Client: owletto-web` (CSRF), then
`POST /api/<orgSlug>/<tool_name>` with the returned cookie.

## Capturing when screenshots cannot be exported
computer-use grants browsers at tier **read**: screenshots yes, scroll/click
**no** — so anything below the fold is unreachable, and the MCP does not hand
back a file path for `save_to_disk`. **Do not fall back to `screencapture`** —
it has no app filtering and grabbed a *peer Claude session's terminal* on the
first try (deleted immediately). Instead extract the rendered DOM with a
throwaway vitest file (untracked files survive `git checkout`, so the same file
runs at both SHAs) and report structure: section headings, badges, and the
COUNT of remove buttons per block. Copy the merged PR's own spec to an untracked
name and run it at the before SHA for a red/green pair.

Related: [[reference_ui_review_needs_a_merged_owletto_pr]] ·
[[feedback_merge_owletto_pr_last_not_first]] ·
[[reference_owletto_submodule_pin_is_not_the_deploy_path]]

content.text:
## What the gap is

It's the same bug we just fixed, one level down.

We fixed the **type** surface: the settings tab listed `member_of` with edit/delete affordances, and every one of those writes 403s. #2837 shipped `purpose` on the type read path, owletto#881 filtered on it, done.

The **edge** surface has the identical problem and is still broken. When the UI lists an entity's relationships, it renders an unlink button per edge. For an ACL-managed edge, `unlink` 403s. Nothing in the response tells the client that.

Here's the proof. `RELATIONSHIP_SELECT` at `packages/server/src/tools/admin/manage_entity.ts:1465` — the shared select behind `list_links` — pulls:

```
rt.slug as relationship_type_slug,
rt.name as relationship_type_name,
rt.is_symmetric,
```

No `purpose`. And `RelationshipRowSchema` (`packages/core/src/contracts/tools/manage-entity.ts:321`) has no field for it either. Meanwhile the guard fires at `manage_entity.ts:1547` for unlink/update_link and `:1599` for link. So the server knows; the client can't.

## Why this isn't just "copy the #2837 fix"

This is the part worth your attention, and it's why I stopped rather than building it.

The two surfaces use **different guards**:

- Type surface → `assertNotAuthorizationType` → `refuseAclManaged(type, action, false)` — **purpose only**
- Edge surface → `assertNotAclManagedEdge` → `refuseAclManaged(type, action, true)` — **purpose OR slug === 'member_of'**

So on edges, a type with `purpose: null` whose slug is `member_of` still 403s. If I shipped `purpose` on the edge row and filtered on it client-side, the UI would still render dead buttons — in exactly the window the slug check exists to cover.

That window is real, not theoretical. The code says so at `relationship-validation.ts:31`:

> A config can declare the `member_of` type before its first ACL sync classifies it; caller-created edges on it are never allowed.

And `examples/personal-agent/lobu.config.ts` legitimately declares `member_of`. So: config applies, type exists with `purpose: null`, first ACL sync hasn't run yet, edges on it are refused. A purpose-only client predicate is wrong for that whole interval.

## Why the client can't just check the slug too

Because the server deliberately hides slug matching behind an explicit `includeSlug` flag, and the docstring says why — it drifts. The entire point of the `purpose` column is to migrate *off* slug matching. Hardcoding `slug === 'member_of'` in Owletto rebuilds the drift-prone thing in the one place we can't update atomically with the server: Owletto is a submodule with its own deploy path, so server and client roll separately. The moment a second authorization slug appears, or `member_of` gets renamed, the client is silently wrong.

We already wrote this rule down in the program memory: never hardcode the slug client-side.

## What I'd propose

The server computes the predicate and returns the answer, not the inputs. A derived boolean on the edge row — call it `acl_managed` — set from the **same** helper the guard uses, so the read path and the enforcement path physically cannot disagree. The client rule becomes "no unlink button when `acl_managed`", and it stays correct when the slug set changes or when classification catches up.

Two things I want your read on:

**The name and its scope.** `acl_managed` says *why* it's refused. An alternative is a capability-shaped name like `can_unlink` that says *what you can do*. I lean toward `acl_managed` because the cross-org public-catalog case is a *different* reason a write fails, and folding both into one `can_*` flag starts a per-row permissions mini-language on every contract. I checked — there's no existing convention for this in `packages/core/src/contracts`, so whichever we pick sets the precedent.

**Whether it's one field or the start of a pattern.** If you'd rather this be a general capability object now, that's a bigger design and I'd want to scope it separately rather than smuggle it in under a bug fix.

Worth noting the adjacent one: task #17, the agent instruction text at `workspace-instructions.ts:88`, is the *type* level, not the edge level — so it's fixable with plain `purpose` and doesn't depend on this decision. It can go independently.

The reason this is a sign-off and not just work: it adds a field to a public contract, and AGENTS.md blocks API/SDK surface changes without your confirmation first — same gate #2837 went through.

Here's how I'd sequence it. Organizing principle: your own stated milestone from the connector-edges interview — **Prodma/ERP end to end, not breadth**. I'm ranking against that rather than by program tidiness.

## Tier 1 — do now, no sign-off needed

**The two write-policy blockers.** These are the highest-value unblocked work in the whole set. Both are reproduced, both have a recommended fix already written down, and both are *prerequisites* for shipping entity write rules — which is what "ERP of record" actually needs.

The first: an approval hold on a field strips the transition, turning a legal write into a denial, and the approval card is never created because `entity-management.ts:1134` returns from inside the transaction before the deferral is built at `:1142`. So the agent's write is denied, misattributed to the wrong cause, *and* dropped with no pending record. A control test proves ownership is the cause, not the rule.

The second: the audit trail is inverted. Successful updates get a field-level diff; creates, deletes, merges, links and unlinks get nothing; and every *denied* write is structurally invisible, because the deny throws, the transaction rolls back, and the audit is post-commit anyway. You get a record when nothing went wrong and nothing when it did. Adding rules makes that strictly worse — every deny becomes a silent failure, and blocker one proves a deny can be flat wrong.

Neither needs a decision from you. They're bugs against a design that's already settled.

One thing I'd do first: the approval-hold repro test is **uncommitted**. Promote it to a regression test before it evaporates. Same for the validation seam at `b56dcd2a1`, which memory says is unpushed — that's fragile.

**Re-cut the Prodma gap register (#10).** Cheap, and its headline verdict is stale. Everything below is being prioritized against a map I don't fully trust — including my own ranking here. I'd do this early precisely so the rest of this list can be corrected.

## Tier 2 — sign-offs I need from you, ranked

**Blocker 1 is taken.** `feat/entity-transitions` has a live session's staged work — a new migration, a rules executor, the `x-transitions` DSL deleted, and `entity-management.ts` edited at 21:26. **So I took #17 instead and it's built.** The agent instruction text now marks ACL-managed relationship types:

```
- member_of (read-only: access control) — Access-control membership
```

Two things worth your attention in how it's done:

It reuses `ACL_MANAGED_TYPE_SQL` — the guard's *own* predicate, already expressed in SQL and documented as expecting the type table aliased `rt`, which this query already does. So there's no second copy of the rule to drift. That matters because the correct predicate here is purpose-**OR**-slug, the same asymmetry we discussed for #16 — a purpose-only test would promise the agent a write it can't make during the window between a config declaring `member_of` and the first ACL sync classifying it.

And the type stays *in* the list rather than being filtered out. Reading those edges is legitimate; hiding the type would just make the agent blind to real schema. Only the write is refused, so the text says exactly that.

Three tests, one per branch, all mutation-proven: narrowing to purpose-only kills the `member_of` case, narrowing to slug-only kills the `grants_role` case, removing the annotation kills both. 29/29 green.

`review-fix` earned its keep and I verified both of its edits rather than taking them: it correctly widened a docstring I'd invalidated, and it deleted a `set_config('lobu.acl_write')` ceremony I'd cargo-culted from my dev-DB seeding. I checked the migration — the trigger is `ON entity_relationships`, not the type table, so the privilege was never needed. Correct on both counts.

It also flagged something I'm not fixing here but you should know about: `global-setup.ts` provides `databaseUrl` via `provide()` precisely because env propagation to forked workers is timing-dependent, but `test-db.ts:95` still reads `process.env.DATABASE_URL` and never calls `inject()`. Under CPU load that turns into "DATABASE_URL is required" and a silent 29-test *skip* — a pass-looking result. On a loaded CI box that's a real hole. I'll file it rather than expand this branch.

**Confidence: high (88)** on the change — real Postgres, real render assertions, both predicate halves mutation-killed, and the guard claim traced to the migration text. The full gate hasn't reported yet, so repo-wide effects are still unproven.

Next up once this merges, and I'd like your steer since one is blocked on you:

1. **#16, the edge predictor** — this branch just proved out the exact predicate it needs, so the design question is now down to the naming call I put to you.
2. **#10, re-cut the Prodma register** — read-only, no collision risk with the peer session, and it fixes the fact that my tiering was stale within the hour.
3. **The vitest `inject()` race** — small, and it currently converts load into a false pass.

I'd default to #10 next since it's collision-free and stops me re-planning from a bad map, unless you want #16's naming settled first so I can build it.

## What

Workspace instructions now mark ACL-managed relationship types as non-writable:

```
- member_of (read-only: access control) — Access-control membership
```

## Why

Arming the ACL guard made every write on an authorization-bearing relationship type 403. The settings UI stopped offering those writes in owletto#881 / #2839, but the **agent-facing** instruction text was still blind — it rendered these types with no hint, so agents kept attempting `link`/`unlink` calls that cannot succeed.

Types are **annotated, not filtered out**. Reading these edges is legitimate, so hiding the type would make the agent blind to real schema. Only the write is refused, so the line says exactly that — the same choice owletto#881 made in the UI.

## The predicate

Reuses `ACL_MANAGED_TYPE_SQL`, the mutation guard's own test, rather than a second copy that can drift. `link`/`unlink` refuse through `assertNotAclManagedEdge`, which is **purpose-OR-slug**. A purpose-only test here would still promise a write the server rejects, during the window between a config declaring `member_of` (as `examples/personal-agent/lobu.config.ts` does) and the first ACL sync classifying it.

The helper's docstring said "for statements that select edges by their type"; widened to cover listing the types themselves.

## Tests

Three cases, one per branch of the OR, so narrowing either half fails the suite:

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| predicate → purpose-only | ✗ `marks the ACL slug read-only even before classification has run` |
| predicate → slug-only | ✗ `marks a CLASSIFIED relationship type read-only` |
| annotation removed | ✗ both |
| unmutated | ✓ 29/29 |

```
Test Files  1 passed (1)

```

Depot gate `nb2dxn2tl8` passed.

## Not in scope

The **edge** surface is still blind: `RelationshipRowSchema` carries no predictor, so *unlink* buttons on an entity's relationships can still 403. That needs a derived boolean on a public contract and is pending owner sign-off.

Separately, `review-fix` surfaced a harness bug worth its own branch: `global-setup.ts` provides `databaseUrl` via `provide()`, but `test-db.ts:95` still reads `process.env.DATABASE_URL` and never calls `inject()`. EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -3

**#2840 is up** — gate passed, review clean (0 blockers), CI settling now. I'll merge when the required contexts report.

While that runs, two things from the review worth your call rather than my assumption:

**A latent hole in what I just shipped.** The inverse-pair dedup loop at `workspace-instructions.ts:118` emits only one side of a paired relationship type. So if an ACL-managed type ever gained an inverse whose name sorts first and which isn't itself classified, the read-only hint would silently vanish. No such pairing exists today, which is why it's not a blocker — but it's a real gap, and the clean fix is to make the pair inherit `acl_managed` from either side rather than from whichever line wins the sort. Small. Say the word and I'll fold it in before merge, or file it.

**A pre-existing one I did not introduce.** The listing query is org-scoped, but `link` also resolves *public-catalog* types. A public `member_of` would 403 without ever appearing in the agent's hint list. That's the same class of bug I just fixed, one scope over.

Also filing the vitest `inject()` race, since it converts CPU load into a false pass rather than a failure:

Observed on 3 consecutive runs while a peer session ran NCPU*3 busy loops; passed again once load eased. A loaded CI box can hit the same thing, so a green run is not currently proof the suite ran. Fix: consume inject() at those read sites. Surfaced by review-fix on #2840.

Two parts, different strength — re-assessed 2026-08-17.

REAL (latent, in code just shipped by #2840): the inverse-pair dedup loop at workspace-instructions.ts:118 emits only one side of a paired relationship type. If an ACL-managed type ever gains an inverse whose name sorts first and which is itself unclassified, the "read-only: access control" hint is dropped. No such pairing exists today. Fix: make the pair inherit acl_managed from EITHER side rather than from whichever line wins ORDER BY name.

WEAKER THAN FIRST FRAMED: the "public-catalog" half. workspace-instructions is org-scoped (`AND rt.organization_id = $1`) while handleLink resolves tenant-then-public-catalog (manage_entity.ts:1577, `OR o.visibility = 'public'`). But an unlisted type is one the agent is not offered at all — it would have to learn the slug elsewhere to attempt the link. So this is closer to a product question (should public-catalog relationship types appear in workspace instructions at all?) than to the dead-affordance bug #2840 fixed. Do not bundle the two.

content.text:
I need to correct something I told you an hour ago.

**#21 isn't a real bug, and I shouldn't have relayed it as one.** I passed on `review-fix`'s framing — "turns load into a silent pass" — without checking it. Verified now:

The silent-self-skip class requires a module-load skip gate. Grepping every server test for `skipIf`/`describe.skip` combined with `DATABASE_URL` returns exactly one hit, and it's the *historical comment* in `table-schema.test.ts` describing the bug that `provide`/`inject` already fixed. No live instances, and no vacuous early-return guards either. Every other suite calls `getTestDb()`, which **throws** — a throw in `beforeAll` is a failed suite and a non-zero exit. The "29 skipped" that `review-fix` saw is just vitest's reporting alongside `Failed Suites 1`; the run still goes red.

What's actually left is a modest flake — fork env propagation is timing-dependent, so heavy load can spuriously red a suite. Visible, not silent. Downgraded rather than built.

**#22 was also half wrong on my part.** The genuinely real piece is the inverse-pair dedup hole in the code I just shipped. The "public-catalog" half is thinner than I said: an unlisted type is one the agent is never offered, so it'd have to learn the slug elsewhere to attempt the link. That's a product question — should public-catalog relationship types appear in workspace instructions at all — not the dead-affordance bug #2840 fixed. I've split them so they don't get bundled.

That leaves #16 as the real next build, and it's genuinely blocked on you:

options.label: acl_managed (Recommended)
options.description: Says WHY the write is refused. Matches the server-side name already in use (ACL_MANAGED_TYPE_SQL, assertNotAclManagedEdge), and leaves room for cross-org catalog types — a different refusal reason — to get their own signal rather than being folded in.

options.label: can_unlink
options.description: Says WHAT the caller can do. Reads more naturally at the call site, but invites every other refusal reason (cross-org catalog, permissions, freeze) to collapse into the same flag — the start of a per-row permissions language on every contract.

## Summary
- `manage_entity` relationship rows now carry a server-derived `acl_managed: boolean`, so a client can tell which edges are refused by `assertNotAclManagedEdge` before it renders an unlink/edit control that is guaranteed to 403.
- The flag is derived, not the raw `purpose`, because the edge guard tests **purpose OR slug**: a `member_of` type declared by a config but not yet classified by an ACL sync reads `purpose: null` and is still refused. Only the server can evaluate that pair, so it ships the answer.
- Same predicate as the guard (`ACL_MANAGED_TYPE_SQL`), projected once from the shared `RELATIONSHIP_SELECT`, so every producer of a relationship row gets it.

Follows #2837 (purpose on the type read surface) and #2840 (`read-only: access control` in the agent's workspace instructions). This is the third and last blind surface from that program: the **edge** rows themselves.

## Test plan
- [x] Intended files staged explicitly, then `make pre-pr-remote` clean
- [x] Tests run: `packages/server/src/__tests__/integration/authz/authorization-type-guards.test.ts` — 17/17 pass
- [ ] Bug fix: red→fix→green outputs pasted below
- [ ] If bot runtime changed

Three tests added to the existing guard suite:
- `acl_managed` is `true` on `LIST_LINKS` for a classified authorization type
- `acl_managed` is `true` **before** classification (`purpose: null`, slug `member_of`) — this is the case a purpose-only field would get wrong
- `acl_managed` is `false` for ordinary domain vocabulary

Mutation-tested: swapping the projection to purpose-only fails the "before classification" test; hardcoding `true as acl_managed` fails the "ordinary domain vocabulary" test. File restored identical after each.

## Notes
`packages/client/src/generated/types.gen.ts` is regenerated output — produced by `bun run generate` in `packages/client` against a booted server, after confirming `acl_managed` was present in the served OpenAPI spec.

The field is required rather than optional: an absent flag reads as writable, which is the dead affordance this exists to remove. All three `sql.unsafe<RelationshipRow>` producers share `RELATIONSHIP_SELECT` + `RELATIONSHIP_JOINS`, which aliases the type table `rt`, so no path can omit it.

Follow-up not in this PR: Owletto still renders unlink controls without consulting the flag — that is a separate submodule change.

name: reference-deployed-prod-sha-from-image-tag
description: "How to resolve which commit is actually running on prod — the image tag's numeric suffix is the 'Build and Push Images' workflow RUN NUMBER, not a SHA"
metadata:

---

The rollout gate in AGENTS step 11 needs a `DEPLOYED_SHA`, but nothing on the
cluster carries one. The deployment image is `ghcr.io/lobu-ai/lobu-app:<TAG>`
with `TAG = YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-NNNNNN`, and there is **no** commit label, env var,
pod label, or annotation exposing the SHA. `/api/v1/health` returns no version
either. Anonymous GHCR manifest pulls fail (private package), so reading
`org.opencontainers.image.revision` off the image is a dead end too.

**`NNNNNN` is the `Build and Push Images` workflow RUN NUMBER.** That is the join key:

```bash
TAG=$(kubectl -n summaries-prod get deploy summaries-app-lobu-app \
  -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}')
N=$(echo "$TAG" | sed 's/.*-0*\([0-9]*\)$/\1/')
DEPLOYED_SHA=$(gh run list --workflow "Build and Push Images" --limit 30 \
  --json number,headSha --jq ".[]|select(.number==$N)|.headSha")
git merge-base --is-ancestor "$MERGE_SHA" "$DEPLOYED_SHA"   # merge commit FIRST
```

Verified 2026-08-08: tag `20260808-025311-001973` → run 1973 → `6c290b5967`,
which is #2590's squash commit.

Two traps. **The three images roll independently** — `lobu-worker` and
`lobu-embeddings` were at run 1974 while `lobu-app` was still on 1973, so gate
on the specific deployment you care about, not "the latest tag". And **the
pod's `AGE` is a better rollout clock than the tag timestamp**: the tag records
when the image was BUILT, Flux picks it up later.

Related: [[feedback_post_merge_prod_verify_wakeup]] ·
[[project_prod_flux_image_automation]] ·
[[project_behavior_output_visibility_2590]]

```bash

```

**The DB pod is `lobu-db-prod-1`** (was `lobu-ai-prod-db-1` before ~2026-08-14;
that name now 404s). Confirm with
`kubectl get pods -n summaries-prod | grep -iE 'db|postgres'` — there is also a
`lobu-db-prod-pooler-*`, which is NOT the exec target. psql warns
`Defaulted container "postgres"`; that is fine.

Three traps, each of which costs a round trip:

1. **The database is `owletto`, not `app`.** `\l` lists both; `app` exists and is
   empty, so `-d app` returns `relation "feeds" does not exist` rather than an
   obvious error. The name is in `DATABASE_URL`'s path segment.
2. **`-h 127.0.0.1` is load-bearing.** Without it psql uses the unix socket and
   the `summaries` role fails peer auth (`Peer authentication failed`). `-U
   postgres` authenticates on the socket but cannot see the app schema.
3. Get the pod name from `kubectl get pods -n summaries-prod` — the app pods are
   `summaries-app-lobu-app-*` and the name changes on every deploy.

Length-assert the password before using it — see
[[feedback_kubectl_printenv_can_silently_return_empty]].

---
name: reference_inverse_type_id_is_display_only_not_an_edge_write_path
description: "entity_relationship_types.inverse_type_id is consulted by NO edge-write path — writing one half never materializes the other, so a straddling ACL pair is a display bug, not an ACL bypass"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
---

Checked 2026-08-17 while fixing the inverse-pair collapse in
`workspace-instructions.ts`. The scary hypothesis was: if `link` on
`has_report` also materialized its inverse `reports_to` edge, then pairing an
ordinary type to an ACL type would be a **write-around** of
`assertNotAclManagedEdge`.

**It is not.** `inverse_type_id` is read by exactly four places, none of them an
edge write:

- `manage_entity_schema.ts` — schema CRUD (`inverse_type_slug` create/update)
- `workspace-instructions.ts` — the agent's vocabulary listing
- `table-schema.ts` — column exposure
- `prune.test.ts`

`manage_entity.ts` (the link/unlink/update_link surface) does not mention
`inverse` at all. So the property is **purely descriptive metadata**: an
assertion that two vocabularies name the same relation, with no materialization
and no guard consequence. ACL reads key on the edge's own
`relationship_type_id`.

## Pairing IS guarded, but only purpose-side

`resolveInverseType` (`manage_entity_schema.ts:915`) calls
`assertNotAuthorizationType` on the inverse — you cannot pair your own type to
an **already-classified** authorization type. That is the purpose-only guard, so
a straddling pair is still reachable two ways:

1. pair while both halves are ordinary, then let the ACL sync classify one half
   (classification sets `purpose` and never touches `inverse_type_id`);
2. pair against an unclassified `member_of` (slug-side, which
   `assertNotAuthorizationType` does not test).

## Prod shape at the time

103 active relationship types, **0** with `inverse_type_id` set, 4 symmetric.
All 4 ACL-managed types are `member_of` with `purpose='authorization'`. So the
whole inverse-collapse branch is dead in prod today — the fix is latent-bug
hygiene, not an incident.

Offered three options (wait for Fable's rolling reset / top up credits / opus

REVIEWER_CLI=claude CLAUDE_REVIEW_MODEL=opus make review

That memory says a quota failure "posts **no verdict**". Half right: it posts no
*verdict*, but it DOES post `pi-review` = **fail** on the PR, which then blocks
the merge until a successful review run overwrites it. So a dry pool is not
merely a non-event on the PR — it leaves a red required status behind.

`make review-fix` on a dry codex prints `(no summary emitted)` and exits 1 while
making **zero** edits — the diffstat afterwards is byte-identical to before.
Easy to misread as "the fixer found nothing." Check the diffstat, then rerun
with `REVIEWER_CLI=claude CLAUDE_REVIEW_MODEL=opus`, which IS fine for

## Summary
- The agent's relationship-type listing collapses an inverse pair to one line, but `acl_managed` is decided **per type**. When the halves disagree, the collapse drops whichever half loses `ORDER BY name ASC` — and if that's the ACL-managed half, the agent never learns the slug exists, let alone that writing it 403s.
- Collapse now happens only when both halves carry the same write rule. Ordinary pairs still collapse; a straddling pair renders both lines, each with its own annotation.
- Follows #2840, which added the `read-only: access control` hint this fix keeps from being silently discarded.

**This is a listing defect, not an ACL bypass.** `inverse_type_id` is read by exactly four places — schema CRUD, this listing, `table-schema.ts`, and one test — and by no edge-write path. `manage_entity.ts` never mentions `inverse`, so writing one half never materializes the other, and ACL reads key on the edge's own `relationship_type_id`.

How a straddling pair is reached: `resolveInverseType` (`manage_entity_schema.ts:915`) calls `assertNotAuthorizationType`, so you cannot pair against an *already-classified* type. But that guard is purpose-only, so the pair can be formed while both halves are ordinary and classified afterwards — classification sets `purpose` and never touches `inverse_type_id`. The fixture is ordered to match that sequence.

## Test plan
- [x] Intended files staged explicitly, then `make pre-pr-remote` clean
- [x] Tests run: `packages/server/src/__tests__/integration/tools/workspace-instructions.test.ts` — 31/31
- [x] Bug fix: red→fix→green outputs pasted below

**Red** (new tests against unfixed code — note the collapse-guard is already green, so only the bug is red):
```
 ❯ src/__tests__/integration/tools/workspace-instructions.test.ts:257:17
   expect(out).toContain('- reports_to (inverse: has_report, read-only: access control) — …')
 Tests  1 failed | 30 passed (31)
```

**Green**:
```
 ✓ src/__tests__/integration/tools/workspace-instructions.test.ts (31 tests) 1106ms
 Tests  31 passed (31)
```

**Mutation-tested, one failure each, neither test vacuous**:
```
### MUTATION 1: unconditional collapse (the original bug)
   × keeps both halves of an inverse pair when only one is access-controlled
      Tests  1 failed | 30 passed (31)
### MUTATION 2: no collapse at all
   × still collapses an inverse pair whose halves share the same write rule
      Tests  1 failed | 30 passed (31)
### RESTORED
      Tests  31 passed (31)
```

## Notes
Reachability: prod has 103 active relationship types and **0** with `inverse_type_id` set, so this branch is currently dead there — latent-bug hygiene, not an incident. It is agent-reachable, though: `manage_entity_schema` accepts `inverse_type_slug` on create/update and back-links the pair.

A slug not yet emitted maps to `undefined`, which never equals a boolean. That is what keeps the first half of a pair from skipping itself, and also what makes a type whose inverse is inactive (the `inv` LEFT JOIN carries no status filter, unlike the outer `rt`) fail toward being shown rather than hidden.

The collapse test asserts *exactly one of the pair survives* rather than naming the winner — which half wins depends on the database's collation, and that isn't the property under test.

STATE: CLOSED
TITLE: Entity identities collide across connections sharing a namespace

## What

`idx_entity_identities_live_unique` is `(organization_id, namespace, identifier) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL` — it does **not** include `connection_id`. Two connections in the same org that share an identity namespace therefore collapse onto one entity.

`db/migrations/00000000000000_baseline.sql:3678`:

```sql
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_entity_identities_live_unique
  ON public.entity_identities USING btree (organization_id, namespace, identifier)
  WHERE (deleted_at IS NULL);
```

## Why it matters

Namespaces come from connector manifests (`attributions[].target.identities[].namespace`), not from anything the platform controls. Two ERP connections against two different tenants both declaring `namespace: 'erp_customer'` will resolve `CARI-001` in tenant A to the entity minted for `CARI-001` in tenant B. Nothing errors — the second connection's attribution silently matches the first connection's entity and merges its traits onto it.

Every generic connector is exposed: `invoice_no`, `customer_code`, `order_id` are all natural namespace names and none of them are globally unique across two systems.

## Reproduction

Reproduced in `packages/server/src/utils/__tests__/derived-edges-spike.test.ts` on branch `feat/spike-derived-edges` (`a8e26a5e6`), test `'two connections sharing an identity namespace COLLIDE onto one entity'`. Two connections, same namespace, same identifier, different `connection_id` → one `entities` row, one `entity_identities` row.

## Options

1. Add `connection_id` to the unique index. Correct, but it changes matching semantics for connectors that *want* cross-connection identity (the same Slack user seen through two connections should stay one person).
2. Namespace-scope at write time — prefix the connector's declared namespace with the connection when the manifest opts in, leaving cross-connection matching available for connectors that declare it.

(2) looks right: whether an identity is global or per-connection is a property of the source system, so the connector should declare it rather than the platform guessing.

Found while spiking connector-declared entity→entity edges; filing separately because it is independent of that work.

result.output:
## Summary
- `IdentityNamespaceDefinition.uniquePerOrg` is a declared hint with **zero consumers**. Two separate in-repo comments already recorded it as dead — `insert-event.ts` ("has carried a dead `uniquePerOrg` knob ever since") and `20260806120010_events_identity_key_index.sql` ("exists, is declared false for `email_domain`, and has never had a consumer").
- It also contradicts the storage it purports to describe. `idx_entity_identities_live_unique` is a blanket unique index over `(organization_id, namespace, identifier)` applying to **every** namespace, so `email_domain` is declared non-unique and enforced unique regardless.
- The contradiction is dormant, not live: nothing writes `email_domain` identities today (its own notes say "Nothing derives it automatically"). But the flag reads like a per-namespace uniqueness control that does not exist, which is actively misleading — see Notes.

## Test plan
- [x] Intended files staged explicitly, then `make pre-pr-remote` clean (Depot run `mxm34ff04q` passed)
- [x] Tests run: `bun test src/__tests__/identity-namespaces.test.ts` — 8/8
- [x] Bug fix: n/a — dead-code removal, red→green below is the guard test
- [ ] If bot runtime changed: n/a

### Guard test

`make review-fix` added a registry-wide assertion that the property cannot come back. Mutation-tested by re-adding `uniquePerOrg: true` to one entry:

```
(fail) identity namespace registry (generic only) > does not expose unenforced per-organization uniqueness hints
 7 pass
 1 fail
```

Restored, 8/8 pass.

## Notes

**Why this is worth deleting rather than leaving.** The flag looks like the answer to #2798 (identities colliding across connections) and is not. `uniquePerOrg` is about **cardinality** — does this value identify one entity or many; `email_domain` is false because many people share a domain. #2798 is about **scope** — does this identifier mean the same thing across connections; `erp_customer` `CARI-001` is a different customer in two different tenants. Those come apart cleanly: `email_domain` is many-per-org but globally meaningful, and a connector-specific key is one-per-connection but not globally meaningful. Wiring #2798 to this flag would scope `email_domain` per connection, which is backwards for it.

**Published surface.** `IdentityNamespaceDefinition` is exported from `@lobu/connector-sdk` (14.22.0, `publishConfig.access: public`), so removing a required property is a type-level break for any external consumer reading `def.uniquePerOrg`. Kept as `refactor:` so release-please cuts a patch rather than forcing a major across the whole train for a flag that never had a consumer, and whose registry is closed and core-owned (connector authors declare namespaces via `ConnectorIdentityModule`, which has no such field). Flagging explicitly so the semver call is deliberate.

**Migrations left untouched.** Two applied migrations mention the flag in comments. They are dated records of why that index was built, and CI forbids modifying applied migrations, so the references stay.

-- migrate:up

-- Authorization-bearing relationship types get an explicit, system-controlled
-- classification.
--
-- The hole this closes: `member_of` is simultaneously an ACL primitive and
-- ordinary domain vocabulary, and `ensureMemberOfType` does not create-or-fail —
-- it does `ON CONFLICT (organization_id, slug) DO UPDATE`, so it ADOPTS a
-- pre-existing active row. An org defining `member_of` in its own `lobu apply`
-- schema for domain modelling would have that type silently promoted into the
-- ACL path. `created_by` cannot distinguish origin: it is NULL on the platform
-- path, and it also becomes NULL when a user is deleted.
--
-- Once ACL reads require this column (a SEPARATE, later deploy — see below), a
-- type that is not classified can never grant access, so forgetting to classify
-- fails CLOSED rather than opening a hole.
ALTER TABLE entity_relationship_types
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS purpose text;

-- DROP first so a partially applied migration can be retried safely. NOT VALID
-- avoids validating under the ADD's stronger table lock; the separate VALIDATE
-- permits normal reads and writes while it checks the existing rows.
ALTER TABLE entity_relationship_types
  DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS entity_relationship_types_purpose_check;

ALTER TABLE entity_relationship_types
  ADD CONSTRAINT entity_relationship_types_purpose_check
  CHECK (purpose IS NULL OR purpose = 'authorization') NOT VALID;

ALTER TABLE entity_relationship_types
  VALIDATE CONSTRAINT entity_relationship_types_purpose_check;

-- DELIBERATELY NOT BACKFILLED HERE. Classification is what arms the trigger, and
-- arming it in this deploy would break the ACL syncs running on pods that have
-- not yet restarted: they write member_of edges without the transaction-local
-- flag, so the trigger would reject them until the rollout drained. Every
-- trusted path that may touch ACL edges learns to set the flag while nothing is
-- classified and the trigger is inert. A follow-up deploy backfills the purpose,
-- by which point every live pod already sets the flag.

-- ROLLOUT ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING. This migration and the ACL writers that set the
-- transaction-local flag must be fully deployed BEFORE classification is
-- backfilled or ACL reads require it. During a rolling deploy an old pod can
-- still create an unclassified `member_of`; if new readers already demanded the
-- classification, that org's members would lose access until the next sync.

-- migrate:down

-- Dropping the column removes the classification the ACL reads will depend on.
-- Safe only in the direction it is written: the follow-up that adds
-- `AND rt.purpose = 'authorization'` to the three visibility gates must be rolled
-- back FIRST, or those gates match nothing and every member loses access.
ALTER TABLE entity_relationship_types
  DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS entity_relationship_types_purpose_check;

ALTER TABLE entity_relationship_types
  DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS purpose;

input.content:
-- migrate:up

-- Identity scope: does an identifier mean the same thing across connections?
--
-- `idx_entity_identities_live_unique` is `(organization_id, namespace,
-- identifier)`, so two connections in the same org that share a namespace
-- collapse onto one entity. Namespaces come from connector manifests, not from
-- anything the platform controls: two ERP connections against two different
-- tenants both declaring `erp_customer` resolve `CARI-001` in tenant A to the
-- entity minted for `CARI-001` in tenant B. Nothing errors — the second
-- connection's attribution silently accretes traits onto the first's entity.
--
-- The fix is NOT to add `connection_id` to the index. That column is
-- PROVENANCE: it records which connection first wrote the row, and it is set on
-- every connector-written identity including ones that are legitimately
-- org-wide. Indexing it would split identities that must stay collapsed — in
-- production today one organization shares `slack_channel_id` across three
-- connections and `slack_user_id` across two, and the same Slack user seen
-- through two connections must remain ONE person.
--
-- So scope gets its own column, written only when the connector declares the
-- namespace connection-scoped. NULL means org-wide, which is every row that
-- exists today.
ALTER TABLE entity_identities
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS scope_connection_id bigint;

-- COALESCE to a sentinel rather than indexing the nullable column directly: in
-- a UNIQUE index NULLs are distinct, so a bare `scope_connection_id` would stop
-- deduplicating the org-wide rows entirely — every re-sync would insert another
-- copy. 0 is safe as the sentinel because `connections.id` is a bigserial and
-- never 0.
--
-- Existing rows all have NULL, so they collapse on exactly the key they
-- collapse on today: this migration is behaviour-preserving on its own, and
-- only a connector declaring `scope: 'connection'` changes any outcome.
DROP INDEX IF EXISTS idx_entity_identities_live_unique;

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_entity_identities_live_unique
  ON entity_identities (organization_id, namespace, identifier, COALESCE(scope_connection_id, 0))
  WHERE deleted_at IS NULL;

-- migrate:down

-- Reversible only while no connection-scoped identities exist. Once two
-- connections hold the same (org, namespace, identifier) under different
-- scopes, restoring the narrower index makes them duplicates and the CREATE
-- fails — which is the correct failure: silently collapsing two different
-- tenants' customers onto one entity is the defect this column exists to
-- prevent, and the rollback must not perform it.
DROP INDEX IF EXISTS idx_entity_identities_live_unique;

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_entity_identities_live_unique
  ON entity_identities (organization_id, namespace, identifier)
  WHERE deleted_at IS NULL;

ALTER TABLE entity_identities
  DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS scope_connection_id;

import pathlib
import sys

ROOT = pathlib.Path('packages')
OLD = 'ON CONFLICT (organization_id, namespace, identifier)'
NEW = 'ON CONFLICT (organization_id, namespace, identifier, COALESCE(scope_connection_id, 0))'

changed = []
for path in ROOT.rglob('*.ts'):
    sp = str(path)
    if '/dist/' in sp or 'node_modules' in sp:
        continue
    text = path.read_text(encoding='utf-8')
    if OLD not in text:
        continue
    n = text.count(OLD)
    path.write_text(text.replace(OLD, NEW), encoding='utf-8')
    changed.append((sp, n))

if not changed:
    sys.exit('MISS: no ON CONFLICT sites found')
total = sum(n for _, n in changed)
for sp, n in sorted(changed):
    print(f'{n}  {sp}')
print('total sites rewritten:', total)

---
name: reference_on_conflict_cannot_infer_a_parameterized_expression_index
description: "ON CONFLICT on an EXPRESSION index must spell the constant as a SQL literal — a bound parameter never matches, and changing that index breaks EVERY ON CONFLICT on the table (10 sites for entity_identities)"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
---

Hit 2026-08-17 adding `scope_connection_id` to `entity_identities` (#2798).

## The parameterization trap

New index:

```sql
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_entity_identities_live_unique
  ON entity_identities (organization_id, namespace, identifier, COALESCE(scope_connection_id, 0))
  WHERE deleted_at IS NULL;
```

Writing the matching `ON CONFLICT` through a postgres.js tagged template
interpolates the constant as a BOUND PARAMETER:

```ts
ON CONFLICT (organization_id, namespace, identifier, COALESCE(scope_connection_id, ${ORG_SCOPE_SENTINEL}))
```

That fails at runtime with:

> there is no unique or exclusion constraint matching the ON CONFLICT specification

Conflict-target inference compares the target expression to the index
expression as parse trees, and a `Param` node is never equal to the index's
`Const` node. The constant must appear as a **literal `0`** in the SQL text;
keep the TS constant for the JS side only, and comment the coupling.

**It failed non-deterministically across suites**, which sent me chasing
parallel-test interference: one suite passed while another errored on the same
function. Do not theorize about test isolation before checking that the SQL
itself can infer.

## The blast radius nobody warns you about

Changing a unique index breaks **every** `ON CONFLICT` naming the old column
list — they no longer match any index. For `entity_identities` that was **10**
sites, only one of which was the file I was editing:

`tools/save_content.ts` · `auth/subject-identities.ts` (x2) ·
`utils/canvas-events.ts` · `utils/promote-keyed-entities.ts` ·
`utils/member-entity.ts` · `runs/eval-cases.ts` · plus 3 in test fixtures.

Grep `ON CONFLICT (<the old column list>)` repo-wide BEFORE running anything;
the local test run for the file you edited will be green and prove nothing.

## Also: an index change can falsify a comment in a file you never touch

`utils/entity-merge.ts` documented "a live loser↔live winner collision on the
same (org, namespace, identifier) is impossible — the unique index forbids two
live rows for one value org-wide." After the change that premise is FALSE (two
scopes = two legal live rows). The conclusion survived for a different reason —
the merge UPDATE sets only `entity_id`/`merged_from_entity_id`/`updated_at`,
none of which are in the index, so repointing a row cannot change its key.
`make review-fix` caught this; verify such claims against the actual SQL rather
than accepting the rewrite.

Related: [[reference_review_fix_finds_real_slop_and_invents_false_facts]] ·
[[feedback_generalize_fix_then_grep_class]]

**#2798 was never fixed.** It was auto-closed as COMPLETED by release-please when #2718 merged — the issue closed one second after the release PR, sweeping up the reference from #2817's changelog. I reopened it with the sign-off and the prod evidence.

**Prod data changed the answer.** Option 1 from the issue (add `connection_id` to the index) would now be a live regression: `org_lobucrm` shares `slack_channel_id` across 3 connections and `slack_user_id` across 2, and those collapses are *correct*. Indexing provenance would split one person into two.

**The blast radius was 10x my estimate.** Changing that unique index breaks every `ON CONFLICT` naming the old column list — 10 sites across `save_content`, `subject-identities`, `canvas-events`, `promote-keyed-entities`, `member-entity`, `eval-cases`, plus fixtures. Only one was in the file I was editing. It also surfaced a subtler bug: interpolating the sentinel through a tagged template makes it a bound parameter, and conflict inference can never match a `Param` to the index's `Const` — which failed *non-deterministically* across suites and briefly sent me chasing test isolation.

I owe you one honesty note: I wrote the fix before the test, so I never saw a natural red. I demonstrated it by mutation instead — neutralizing `spec.scope` reproduces the exact #2798 collision (2 tenants → 1 entity), and scoping everything breaks the Slack collapse. Both directions die to distinct tests. That's equivalent evidence, but it isn't the ordering AGENTS asks for, and I'll say so in the PR.

`review-fix` was killed mid-pass, so I reviewed every hunk myself rather than trusting it. Its best catch was in `entity-merge.ts`, a file I never touched: my index change falsified its stated invariant. The conclusion survived for a different reason, which I verified against the actual UPDATE.

content.text:
Those are all deliberate negative-path logs from passing tests, not the cause. The retry is still in flight. Answering your two questions directly.

## Design confidence: 85 on the core, with three unresolved edges

What I'd defend strongly:

The **rejection of option 1** is the best-evidenced decision here, and it's evidence you didn't have when you filed the issue. Adding `connection_id` to the index would today split `org_lobucrm`'s `slack_channel_id` across 3 connections and `slack_user_id` across 2 — collapses that are correct. That's not a judgment call, it's live data.

The **storage shape** is structurally behavior-preserving: every existing row has `scope_connection_id IS NULL`, coalesces to the same sentinel, and collapses on exactly the key it collapses on today. And **`extractLink` is a genuine chokepoint** — matching and insertion both read scope off the identity, so they can't disagree.

Where I'm *not* confident, and these are design questions, not implementation details:

**1. Scope is declared per-usage, not per-namespace.** `EntityIdentitySpec` lives inside each attribution rule, so a connector declaring `erp_customer` across two event kinds can give them different scopes. Nothing validates it. The same value then gets written twice — once scoped, once not — and silently becomes two entities. Fix is either a preflight check (one scope per namespace per connector) or moving the declaration up to the namespace level. **I did not solve this.**

**2. No story for changing scope after data exists.** Ship `scope: 'connection'` on a connector that already wrote org-scoped rows and the same identifier forks: old rows keep NULL, new writes carry a connection id, nothing matches. No backfill, no detection. The first ERP connector that gets this wrong on the first try eats it.

**3. Reconnect duplicates everything — this one I'd fix before building on it.** `scope_connection_id` deliberately has no FK. Delete a connection and reconnect, and `connections.id` changes; every connection-scoped row is stranded and the new connection re-mints the entire customer list as new entities. The migration comment calls this "inert," which is true of the row and false of the outcome. Reconnecting is a routine operation. Scope probably wants to key on something stabler than the row id — a per-connection external account key — or the delete path needs to re-scope.

So: the mechanism is right, the storage is right, and the thing you asked me to decide is decided. But #3 is a real flaw in what I built, and I'd rather say that now than have it surface in prod.

## How close: the PR is ~90% done

15 files, migration, SDK property, chokepoint, all 10 `ON CONFLICT` sites, 3 tests. 1772 local tests green, typecheck clean. What's left is gate → review → merge → prod-verify. If the retry comes back green that's under an hour, most of it waiting.

## On handing off to opencode

Good fit for the mechanical remainder — #12/#13, and Owletto consuming `acl_managed`. But be aware what actually made *this* task hard, because it's what a fresh agent reliably misses:

The work wasn't the feature, it was **invisible blast radius**. Changing one unique index broke `ON CONFLICT` in 10 places, only one of which was the file being edited. content.text: Two real defects, both from the same root: the field is required, but `undefined` (not `null`) reaches the SQL and stringifies to `"undefined"`. And `tsconfig` excludes `__tests__`, so the compiler never flagged the callers. Fixing the type to make `undefined` mean org scope:

input.command:
python3 - <<'PY'
import pathlib
p = pathlib.Path('packages/server/src/utils/entity-link-upsert.ts')
s = p.read_text(encoding='utf-8')

old = """   * Carried on the identity rather than read from params at each use site so
   * matching and insertion cannot disagree: `lookupMatches` and
   * `insertIdentities` both key on this value, and a rule that scopes one of
   * its namespaces but not another produces a mixed array here.
   */
  scopeConnectionId: number | null;"""
new = """   * Carried on the identity rather than read from params at each use site so
   * matching and insertion cannot disagree: `lookupMatches` and
   * `insertIdentities` both key on this value, and a rule that scopes one of
   * its namespaces but not another produces a mixed array here.
   *
   * OPTIONAL, and `undefined` is treated exactly as `null`. Callers outside the
   * attribution path (`resolveSenderIdentity`, tests) hand-build identities and
   * legitimately mean org scope; requiring the field would break them without
   * the compiler noticing, because the server tsconfig excludes `__tests__`.
   * Omission is safe in the only direction that matters: it can never
   * accidentally CLAIM a connection scope, only decline one.
   */
  scopeConnectionId?: number | null;"""
assert old in s, 'MISS ResolvedIdentity'
s = s.replace(old, new, 1)

old2 = "function scopeKeyOf(identity: { scopeConnectionId: number | null }): number {"
new2 = "function scopeKeyOf(identity: { scopeConnectionId?: number | null }): number {"
assert old2 in s, 'MISS scopeKeyOf'
s = s.replace(old2, new2, 1)

old3 = """function identityKey(identity: {
  namespace: string;
  identifier: string;
  scopeConnectionId: number | null;
}): string {"""
new3 = """function identityKey(identity: {
  namespace: string;
  identifier: string;
  scopeConnectionId?: number | null;
}): string {"""
assert old3 in s, 'MISS identityKey'
s = s.replace(old3, new3, 1)

# The SQL array: `undefined` must serialize as NULL, not the string "undefined".
old4 = """  const scopes = params.identities.map((i) => i.scopeConnectionId);"""
new4 = """  // `== null` catches undefined as well as null. A strict `=== null` let an
  // omitted scope through as String(undefined) === "undefined", which Postgres
  // rejects with `invalid input syntax for type bigint`.
  const scopes = params.identities.map((i) => i.scopeConnectionId ?? null);"""
assert old4 in s, 'MISS scopes map'
s = s.replace(old4, new4, 1)

p.write_text(s, encoding='utf-8')
print('ok')
PY

Correcting my last answer: **the gate was red, not green.** I misread it — the "exit code 0" in the notification was my trailing `echo`, not `make`. My notes warn about exactly that and I still walked into it.

It caught two real defects, both mine:

**`scopeConnectionId: undefined` reached Postgres as the string `"undefined"`** and blew up `insertIdentities` with `invalid input syntax for type bigint`. Callers outside the attribution path — `resolveSenderIdentity`, tests — hand-build identities and legitimately mean org scope. I'd made the field required, and the compiler never told me because **the server tsconfig excludes `__tests__`**. The field is now optional with `undefined` treated as org scope, which is safe in the only direction that matters: omission can decline a connection scope, never accidentally claim one.

**A `toEqual` shape assertion** in `sender-identity.test.ts` — a bun test, which my vitest-only local sweep never ran.

That second one is the process lesson: I ran 1772 vitest tests and reported them as if they were coverage. They weren't — the whole bun surface was untouched, and that's precisely where both failures lived.

This sharpens my answer on handing work to opencode. The design is still 85 and the three gaps I named are still the real risks — reconnect-duplication most of all. But the thing that keeps biting on this task isn't design, it's that **the feedback loop lies unless you run the actual gate**. Local green here meant very little twice in a row: first the `ON CONFLICT` inference failing non-deterministically, now a whole test runner I'd skipped.

So if opencode picks this up, the constraint I'd hand over is: the gate is the only source of truth, and `make pre-pr-remote`'s exit code must be read from `make`, not from a trailing command.

input.content:
## Summary
- Two connections in one org that share an identity namespace collapsed onto one entity. `erp_customer` `CARI-001` in ERP tenant A resolved to the entity minted for `CARI-001` in tenant B, and the second connection's attribution silently accreted its traits onto the first's entity. Nothing errored.
- Scope is now **declared per identity namespace**: `EntityIdentitySpec.scope?: 'organization' | 'connection'`, defaulting to `organization`. Only the connector knows whether its namespace is globally meaningful — nothing about `invoice_no` or `customer_code` tells the platform.
- `entity_identities` gains a nullable `scope_connection_id`, written only when a connector declares connection scope. The live-unique index becomes `(organization_id, namespace, identifier, COALESCE(scope_connection_id, 0)) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL`.

Reopens and closes #2798, which was auto-closed as COMPLETED by release-please when #2718 merged (issue closed `16:35:41Z`, release PR merged `16:35:40Z`) — it swept up the reference from #2817's changelog text. Nothing had shipped.

### Why not `connection_id` in the index (issue option 1)

That column is **provenance** — it records which connection first wrote the row, and it is set on every connector-written identity including legitimately org-wide ones. Indexing it splits identities that must stay collapsed. In production today:

| namespace | distinct connections | rows |
|---|---|---|
| `slack_channel_id` | 3 | 9 |
| `slack_user_id` | 2 | 8 |

Those collisions are **correct** — the same Slack user seen through two connections must remain one person. Option 1 would split that person into 2 entities and that channel into 3. The prod data argues for the declared-property design rather than merely permitting it.

Distinct from the `uniquePerOrg` flag deleted in #2817, which was **cardinality** (does this value name one entity or many — `email_domain` names many). Scope is orthogonal: `email_domain` is many-per-org yet globally meaningful, so scoping it per connection would be backwards.

## Test plan
- [x] Intended files staged explicitly, then `make pre-pr-remote` clean (Depot run `3jqr1glq60` passed)
- [x] Tests run: new `identity-connection-scope.test.ts` 3/3; `entity-write-pool-starvation` 2/2; bun `sender-identity` 5/5; 1772 vitest across connectors/events/auth/utils
- [x] Bug fix: red→green below

### red → green

I wrote the fix before the test, so there was no natural red run — the defect is "an intent the manifest could not express." Red is demonstrated by mutation instead, one mutation per direction, each killing exactly one test:

```
### MUTATION 1: ignore spec.scope (== origin/main behavior for this path)
   × keeps a connection-scoped identifier separate across two connections
      Tests  1 failed | 2 passed (3)
### MUTATION 2: scope EVERYTHING per connection
   × still collapses an org-scoped identifier across the same two connections
      Tests  1 failed | 2 passed (3)
### RESTORED
      Tests  3 passed (3)
```

Mutation 1 reproduces the exact #2798 collision: two ERP tenants, one entity.

### Two defects the gate caught that local runs did not

1. `scopeConnectionId: undefined` (not `null`) reached the array literal as `String(undefined)`, and Postgres rejected it with `invalid input syntax for type bigint: "undefined"`. Callers outside the attribution path (`resolveSenderIdentity`, tests) hand-build identities and legitimately mean org scope. The field is now optional, with `undefined` treated as org scope — safe in the only direction that matters, since omission can decline a connection scope but never accidentally claim one. The compiler did not catch this because the server tsconfig excludes `__tests__`.
2. A `toEqual` shape assertion in the **bun** suite `sender-identity.test.ts`, which a vitest-only local sweep never runs.

## Notes

**Blast radius.** Changing the unique index breaks every `ON CONFLICT` naming the old column list — they no longer match any index. That was **10 sites**, only one of which was in the file being edited: `save_content`, `subject-identities` (x2), `canvas-events`, `promote-keyed-entities`, `member-entity`, `eval-cases`, plus 3 in test fixtures.

**The sentinel must be a SQL literal.** Conflict-target inference compares parse trees, so an interpolated `COALESCE(scope_connection_id, $n)` never matches the index's `Const` and fails with *"there is no unique or exclusion constraint matching the ON CONFLICT specification"* — non-deterministically across suites, which reads exactly like test-isolation flake.

**No foreign key on `scope_connection_id`, deliberately.** `ON DELETE SET NULL` would silently promote a connection-scoped identity to org-wide — the exact collapse the column prevents — and could collide with a legitimately org-wide row. `CASCADE` would delete identity rows and take their entities' attribution with them.

**`entity-merge.ts` documented an invariant this change falsifies.** It claimed a live loser↔winner collision on the same `(org, namespace, identifier)` was impossible because the index forbids two live rows for one value org-wide. Two scopes now make two live rows legal. The conclusion survives for a different reason — the merge UPDATE sets only `entity_id`/`merged_from_entity_id`/`updated_at`, none of which are in the index — so the comment is corrected rather than the code.

**Behaviour-preserving on its own.** Every existing row has `scope_connection_id IS NULL` and collapses on exactly the key it collapses on today. Only a connector declaring `scope: 'connection'` changes any outcome, and none do yet.

### Known gaps, filed separately

- Scope is declared per *usage*, not per namespace: a connector declaring the same namespace in two event kinds with different scopes silently produces two entities. No validation.
- No story for changing a namespace's scope after rows exist — the identifier forks.
- Deleting and re-creating a connection changes `connections.id`, stranding connection-scoped rows so the new connection re-mints its entities. Reconnecting is routine, so this is the one that produces bad prod data.
